blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: In this paper, we prove that, unless P=NP, no polynomial-time algorithm can find a tokeniser whose objective is within any constant factor of the optimum, meaning that tokenisation is not in the APX complexity class. We prove this for direct and bottom-up tokenisation, under both a compression or unigram log-likelihood objectives, and for binary or larger alphabets. We further show that, even over unary alphabets, direct tokenisation is APX-hard, and thus admits no polynomial-time approximation scheme.
blocks.zh: 在本文中,我们证明,除非P=NP,否则任何多诺时算法都找不到一个指向器,其目标在任意最优的恒定因子范围内,意味着指向不是APX复杂类. 我们证明这是直接的和自下而上的, 在一个压缩或Ungram日志相似的目标下, 对于二进制或更大的字母表。 我们进一步表明,即使超过非专用字母表,直接的表示式是APX-hard,因此不接受多名时间近似方案.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Tokenisers are the “glasses” through which language models (LMs) see the world, converting raw text—made of bytes or characters—into sequences of tokens.
They define an LM’s API costs,
impact the models’ throughput,
affect their performance, and
directly shape output distributions ( Zouhar et al., 2023 ; Lesci et al., 2025 ; Ahia et al., 2023 ) .
It is thus natural to pose the question: how should one choose a tokeniser? A recent line of research frames this question as an optimisation problem:
define an objective function, and find a tokeniser that performs well on it.
In fact, famous tokenisation algorithms can be seen as instantiations of this principle. BPE is a greedy algorithm for compression, iteratively merging the most frequent pair of adjacent tokens ( Gage, 1994 ; Sennrich et al., 2016 ) , while UnigramLM is an expectation-maximisation algorithm for log-likelihood ( Kudo, 2018 ; Meister, 2026 ) .
Notably, these methods are purely heuristic, having no guarantees regarding their solutions’ quality. 1 1 1 BPE , in particular, can have arbitrarily bad compression ( Kozma and Voderholzer, 2026 ) . See Yavuz et al. (2026) for an analysis of how these methods’ objective functions and optimisation algorithms interact when selecting a tokeniser.
blocks.zh:
Tokenisers是语言模型(LMs)通过它看到世界的"镜",将原始文本——由字节或字符所制作——转换成符号序列.
他们定义了LM的API成本,
影响模型的吞吐量,
影响其业绩,以及
直接形状输出分布 (Zouhar等,2023;Lesci等,2025;Ahia等,2023.).
因此,提出这样一个问题是自然的:人们应该如何选择一个象征性的? 最近一行研究将这个问题作为优化问题:
定义一个客观的函数,并找到一个能很好地执行它的符号。
事实上,出名的象征化算法可以被看作这一原则的即时论. BPE是一款用于压缩的贪婪算法,迭接地将相邻最频繁的一对相邻的符相(Gage,1994;Sennrich等,2016;而UnigramLM是一款用于日志相近的预期-最大化算法(Kudo,2018;Meister,2026).
值得注意的是,这些方法纯粹是高压的,无法保证其解决方案的质量。 特别是11 1 BPE(Kozma和Voderholzer, 2026年 ) , 可能任意的压缩不良。 见Yavuz等人(2026年),关于这些方法的客观功能和优化算法在选择指示器时如何相互作用的分析。

blocks.en:
A few recent works have explored whether it is even possible to propose tokenisers with optimality guarantees—all focusing on compression as their analysed objective.
Studying unboundedly large alphabets, a set of initial papers proved that tokenisation’s optimisation problem is 𝖭𝖯 \mathsf{NP} -hard ( Whittington et al., 2025 ; Kozma and Voderholzer, 2026 ; Lim et al., 2025 ) . 2 2 2 More precisely, Whittington et al. (2025) showed that both direct and bottom-up tokenisation are 𝖭𝖯 \mathsf{NP} -complete, Kozma and Voderholzer (2026) showed that bottom-up tokenisation, with or without partial merges, is 𝖠𝖯𝖷 \mathsf{APX} -hard, and Lim et al. (2025) showed that direct tokenisation is 𝖭𝖯 \mathsf{NP} -hard. Follow up work then showed it is still 𝖭𝖯 \mathsf{NP} -hard over unary alphabets, and 𝖠𝖯𝖷 \mathsf{APX} -hard over binary ones ( Kastreva et al., 2026 ) . 3 3 3 Explicitly, 𝖠𝖯𝖷 \mathsf{APX} -hardness means that, for some constant c > 1 c>1 , no polynomial-time algorithm can guarantee a solution within a factor c c of the optimum, unless 𝖯 = 𝖭𝖯 \mathsf{P}=\mathsf{NP} . These results, however, leave open three main questions: (i) is tokenisation hard for other objectives beyond compression?
(ii) does any constant-factor approximation algorithm exist for tokenisation?
(iii) is unary tokenisation also hard to approximate?
blocks.zh:
最近的一些著作探讨了是否有可能提出具有最佳性保证的标志物——所有这些都侧重于压缩,作为其分析的目标。
在研究无限制的大字母表时,一套初步论文证明,象征化的优化问题在于NP\mathsf{NP}-hard(Whittington等,2025年;Kozma和Voderholzer,2026年;Lim等,2025年)。 2更精确地说,惠特廷顿等人(2025年)显示,直接和自下而上的表示式是NP\mathsf{NP}-完成式,克兹马和沃德霍尔泽(2026年)显示,无论是否部分合并,自下而上表示式是APX\mathsf{APX}-hard,和Lim等人. (2025) 显示直接的符号化为 NP\ mathsf{ NP} - 硬. 后续工作显示它仍然是 NP \ mathsf{ NP} - 硬于 unary 字母表, 而 APX\ mathsf{ APX}} - 硬于 二进制字母表 (Kastreva等, 2026). 3 3 明确, APX \ mathsf{ APX}- 硬度表示,对于一些常数 c > 1 c> 1, 任何多时算法都无法保证在最优的c因子 c 内求解, 除非 P= NP \ mathsf{ P}=\mathsf{ NP}. 然而,这些结果留下了三个主要问题:(一) 对压缩之外的其他目标来说,表示很难吗?
(二) 是否存在用于表示的常因近似算法?
(三) 无名证也很难估计吗?

blocks.en:
In this work, we tackle these three questions.
First, we answer (i) and (ii) showing that binary tokenisation is not in 𝖠𝖯𝖷 \mathsf{APX} ; we prove this for direct and bottom-up tokenisation, covering both the compression and unigram log-likelihood objectives.
This means that, unless 𝖯 = 𝖭𝖯 \mathsf{P}=\mathsf{NP} , no polynomial-time algorithm can approximate binary tokenisation within any constant factor, under either objective. 4 4 4 Concurrently, Baliga et al. (2026) showed this for bottom-up tokenisation, and Ion et al. (2026) and Bastan et al. (2026) for direct tokenisation, all under a compression objective. Second, we answer (iii) by proving that unary tokenisation is 𝖠𝖯𝖷 \mathsf{APX} -hard—so even in such simple alphabets, tokenisation cannot be approximated arbitrarily well (shown in App. C due to space). Figure 1 summarises prior results and ours.
blocks.zh:
在这项工作中,我们处理这三个问题。
首先,我们回答(一)和(二),显示二进制符号不在APX\mathsf{APX}}中;我们证明这一点是为了直接和自下而上地表示符号,既包括压缩目标,也包括Unigram日志相似目标.
这意味着,除非 P = NP\ mathsf{ P}=\mathsf{ NP},任何多名时算法都不能在任何常数内,在任一目标下,大致表示二进制. 页:1 4 同时,Baliga等人(2026年)在自下而上地表示这一点,而Ion等人(2026年)和Bastan等人(2026年)在直接表示这一点,都列在压缩目标之下。 第二,我们回答(三) 证明无符号化是 APX\ mathsf{ APX}--hard-所以即使用这种简单的字母表,也不能任意地将符号化做得很好(由于空间原因在 App. C 中出现)。 图1总结了以往的成果和我们的成果。

blocks.en:
Overall, our results rule out the existence of (unconditional) approximation algorithms for tokenisation. 5 5 5 In fact, for compression, our bounds nearly match those achieved by trivial character-level tokenisers. Guarantees for practical tokenisers must therefore be dataset-specific, rather than hold for all possible inputs.
In fact, in practice, tokenisers perform fairly well when applied to natural languages, coming within about 1 % 1\% of the optimal compression ( Tempus et al., 2026 ) .
Future work should explore what makes natural language so much easier to tokenise than our worst-case constructions, and explore data-specific algorithmic guarantees.
blocks.zh:
总体而言,我们的结果排除了(无条件的)近似算法的存在,用于表示. 5 5 5 事实上,为了压缩,我们的界限 几乎与小的字符级标志器所达到的界限相匹配。 因此,对实用符号的保证必须是针对数据集的,而不是针对所有可能的投入。
事实上,在实际操作中,在适用于自然语言时,标志剂的性能相当好,在最佳压缩的1%以内(Tempus等人,2026年)。
未来的工作应该探索是什么使得自然语言比我们最坏的构造更容易表征,并探索数据特定的算法保证.

blocks.en: 2.1 Tokenisation Objectives
blocks.zh: 2.1 切入目标

blocks.en:
Although no perfect objective seems to exist for tokenisation, several functions are said to correlate with a tokeniser’s performance: e.g., unigram log-likelihood ( Kudo, 2018 ) , 95%-ile token frequency ( Gowda and May, 2020 ) , Rényi efficiency ( Zouhar et al., 2023 ) , and compression ( Gallé, 2019 ) .
It is thus natural to use them as an objective for tokenisation.
We analyse two of them here.
blocks.zh:

blocks.en: 3 Direct Tokenisation is not in 𝗔𝗣𝗫 \mathsf{APX}
blocks.zh: 3 直接切入不包含在 APX\ mathsf{ APX}}

blocks.en:
We now prove that direct tokenisation is not in the 𝖠𝖯𝖷 \mathsf{APX} class.
We do so using a gap reduction from a known 𝖭𝖯 \mathsf{NP} -hard problem, finite-word rank, to binary direct tokenisation.
From an instance of this 𝖭𝖯 \mathsf{NP} -hard decision problem —whose desired output is a 𝖸𝖤𝖲 \mathsf{YES} or 𝖭𝖮 \mathsf{NO} answer—we build an instance of the tokenisation optimisation problem whose optimal objective will be small if the answer to the finite-word rank instance is 𝖸𝖤𝖲 \mathsf{YES} , and large if it is 𝖭𝖮 \mathsf{NO} .
By making this gap arbitrarily large, we then show that any constant-factor approximation to tokenisation would allow us to distinguish 𝖸𝖤𝖲 \mathsf{YES} from 𝖭𝖮 \mathsf{NO} answers in finite-word rank. 9 9 9 Gap reductions are a classic technique, used, e.g., to show that the general travelling salesman problem admits no constant-factor approximation ( Sahni and Gonzalez, 1976 ) . Unless 𝖯 = 𝖭𝖯 \mathsf{P}=\mathsf{NP} , this is thus infeasible in polynomial time.
Notably, proving the hardness of tokenisation with | Σ | = 2 |{\color[rgb]{0.3281,0.4961,0.9375}\Sigma}|=2 also proves it for all | Σ | > 2 |{\color[rgb]{0.3281,0.4961,0.9375}\Sigma}|>2 .

我们这样做是使用从已知的 NP \ mathsf{ NP} - 硬性问题, 限定字级, 到二进制直接符号化 来缩小差距 。
从这个 NP \ mathsf{ NP} - 硬性决定问题—— 想要输出为 YES \ mathsf{ YES} 或 NO\ mathsf{ NO} 答案的例子中, 我们构建了一个标志性优化问题的例子, 如果对限定词的回答是 YES \ mathsf{ YES} , 其最佳目标将是小的, 如果是 NO\ mathsf{ NO} 。
通过任意使这一差距扩大,我们然后显示,任何恒定因素近似于表示性,将使我们能够在限定词名中区分YES\mathsf{YES}和NO\mathsf{NO}答案。 9 9 缩小差距是一种经典技术,用来表明一般旅行推销员问题不接受常因近似(Sahni和Gonzalez,1976年)。 除非 P = NP \ mathsf{ P}=\mathsf{ NP},否则在多诺时段内无法执行 。

The finite-word rank problem is closely related to tokenisation, but differs in two main ways.
First, 𝒴 \mathcal{Y} need not contain Σ wr \Sigma_{\texttt{wr}} , allowing for solutions that cannot represent all strings in Σ wr ∗ \Sigma_{\texttt{wr}}^{*} .
Second, it asks about the size of 𝒴 \mathcal{Y} , instead of how compactly 𝒳 \mathcal{X} can be represented using tokens in 𝒴 \mathcal{Y} .
Leveraging these differences will be the key to our results.

blocks.en: 4 Bottom-up Tokenisation is not in 𝗔𝗣𝗫 \mathsf{APX}
blocks.zh: 4 自下而上 Tokenisation 不属于 APX \ mathsf{ APX}}

blocks.en:
We now show that binary bottom-up tokenisation is also not in the 𝖠𝖯𝖷 \mathsf{APX} class, under either objective.
To this end, we will reduce from maximum cut on cubic graphs .
Here, we rely on a gap amplification reduction .
Our reduction outputs a single binary string which collapses into one token within the budget on 𝖸𝖤𝖲 \mathsf{YES} instances, but keeps a growing number of tokens on 𝖭𝖮 \mathsf{NO} instances. 10 10 10 Notably, this reduction amplifies the gap of the 𝖯𝖢𝖯 \mathsf{PCP} theorem ( Arora and Safra, 1998 ; Arora et al., 1998 ; Dinur, 2007 ) .
Known reductions carry this gap over to maximum cut on cubic graphs ( Håstad, 2001 ; Berman and Karpinski, 2001 ) .

为此,我们将从立方图上的最大切入量减少。
在这里,我们依靠缩小差距。
我们的减值输出一个二进制字符串,在预算范围内,该字符串在"是"\ mathsf{YES}实例上崩溃成一个符号,但在"是"实例上却保留了越来越多的符号在"NO\ mathsf{NO}实例上. 10 值得注意的是,这一减值扩大了五氯苯酚\mathsf{PCP}定理的差距(Arora和Safra,1998年;Arora等人,1998年;Dinur,2007年).
已知的减排量将这一差距延伸到了立方图的最大截取量(Håstad,2001;Berman和Karpinski,2001)。

5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
In this work, we proved that binary tokenisation is not in 𝖠𝖯𝖷 \mathsf{APX} , and that unary direct tokenisation is 𝖠𝖯𝖷 \mathsf{APX} -hard.
In fact, our reductions leave open only relatively trivial approximation guarantees, close in approximation ratio to, e.g., character-level tokenisation.
Any practical approximation guarantee for tokenisers must thus be dataset-specific.
Future work should thus seek such conditional guarantees, e.g., by certifying how close a tokeniser is to optimal on a given target dataset. 11 11 11 A first step towards this goal was done by Tempus et al. (2026) using linear programming.
blocks.zh:
在这部作品中,我们证明了二进制符号不是在 APX \ mathsf{ APX}} 中,而无活性直接符号是 APX\mathsf{ APX} - 硬.
事实上,我们的削减额只留下相对微不足道的近似保证,接近于性格层面的标识。
因此,任何实际近似担保都必须针对数据集。
因此,今后的工作应当寻求这种有条件的保证,例如,通过证明一个标志器对特定目标数据集的最佳程度。 11 11 Tempus等人(2026年)利用线性编程为实现这一目标迈出了第一步。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en:
Our hardness results rely on carefully constructed datasets, which differ substantially from natural text; our results thus say little about the natural-language datasets tokenisers are trained on, where current algorithms may be near-optimal.
Further, our analysis covers two objectives, compression and unigram log-likelihood, and two kinds of tokenisers, direct and bottom-up;
other objectives, such as Rényi efficiency, and other variants, such as those allowing partial merges ( Kozma and Voderholzer, 2026 ) , remain open.
We suspect, however, that most interesting classes of tokenisers and objective functions will also be hard to approximate.
blocks.zh:
我们的硬度结果依赖于精心构建的数据集,这些数据集与自然文本大相径庭;因此,我们的结果对自然语言数据集的表示器几乎没有什么意义,因为当前的算法可能接近最佳。
此外,我们的分析包括两个目标:压缩和一克对数法,以及两种象征性方法,直接和自下而上;
其他目标,如Rényi效率,以及允许部分合并的其他变体(Kozma和Voderholzer,2026年),仍然开放。
然而,我们怀疑,最令人感兴趣的类示意者和客观功能也很难估计。

blocks.en: Appendix B Proof that Binary Bottom-up Tokenisation is not in 𝗔𝗣𝗫 \mathsf{APX}
blocks.zh: 附录B 证明二进制自下而上 Tokenization 不在 APX\ mathsf{ APX} 中

blocks.en:
This appendix proves Theorem 3 and Theorem 4 .
Both follow from a single reduction from gap maximum cut on cubic graphs, and from the gap it creates, which we state as a forward and a backward implication ( Proposition 1 ).
Taking this gap as given, § B.1 and § B.2 first prove the two theorems.
The remaining subsections build up to Proposition 1 : § B.3 recalls maximum cut on cubic graphs, § B.4 constructs the reduction, and § B.5 states the gap.
Finally, § B.6 turns a maximum cut into a short merge sequence that collapses the encoded string into a single token, and § B.7 shows that no merge sequence over the binary alphabet can do better.
blocks.zh:
本附录证明定理3和定理4.
两者都来自从立方图上的最大相距缩小一次,以及从它造成的相距缩小一次,我们说这是一种前向和后向的影响(提议1 )。
照此规定,§B.1和§B.2首先证明了这两个定理.
其余各分节累积到提案1:§B.3回顾了立方图上的最大切入量,§B.4构建了还原量,而§B.5则说明了差距.
最后,§B.6将一个最大切成一个短的合并序列来将被编码的字符串倒塌成单一的符号,而§B.7显示,任何二进制字母上方的合并序列都不能做得更好.

Part (c) holds since consecutive walks are separated by a separator.
For part (a) , note that separators are never adjacent to each other, and that # {\color[rgb]{0.3281,0.4961,0.9375}\#} occurs only once.
A bigram consisting of a vertex v {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}v} followed by a separator ⋄ χ {\color[rgb]{0.3281,0.4961,0.9375}\diamond_{\chi}} marks the end of a walk which ends in v {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}v} ; by our choice of separators, no other walk ending in v {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}v} is followed by ⋄ χ {\color[rgb]{0.3281,0.4961,0.9375}\diamond_{\chi}} , so this bigram occurs only once.
The same holds, symmetrically, for a separator followed by a vertex.
For part (b) , it suffices to consider substrings of length exactly 3 3 , as longer substrings contain one.
A substring of length 3 3 containing a separator or # {\color[rgb]{0.3281,0.4961,0.9375}\#} contains a bigram from part (a) , and thus occurs only once.
Otherwise, its three symbols are vertices, which by part (c) lie in the same walk; as walks have length 3 3 , the substring is a walk, and walks are pairwise distinct.

Phase 1: merging bigrams ( Fig. 4(c) ). For every arc ( v , v ′ ) ∈ 𝒰 ⋆ ({\color[rgb]{0,0,0}v},{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}v}^{\prime})\in{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\mathcal{U}}^{\star} , in arbitrary order, we merge v ⊚ v ′ {\color[rgb]{0.8633,0.1484,0.4961}{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}v}}\mathbin{{\color[rgb]{0.8633,0.1484,0.4961}\circledcirc}}{\color[rgb]{0.8633,0.1484,0.4961}{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}v}^{\prime}} .
By Lemma 5 (c) , two adjacent vertices only occur inside walks, and since v ≠ v ′ {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}v}\neq{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}v}^{\prime} , the occurrences of the pair never overlap.
So a merge v ⊚ v ′ {\color[rgb]{0.8633,0.1484,0.4961}{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}v}}\mathbin{{\color[rgb]{0.8633,0.1484,0.4961}\circledcirc}}{\color[rgb]{0.8633,0.1484,0.4961}{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}v}^{\prime}} only changes the walks which have ( v , v ′ ) ({\color[rgb]{0,0,0}v},{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}v}^{\prime}) as a bigram.
Once one bigram of a walk is merged, the walk’s middle vertex lies inside a token of two symbols, and no later merge of this phase changes the walk.
As 𝒰 ⋆ {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\mathcal{U}}^{\star} covers all walks, every walk is shortened by exactly one token.
This phase uses | 𝒰 ⋆ | |{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\mathcal{U}}^{\star}| merges and leaves | 𝐰 | − M = 3 ​ M + 1 |{\color[rgb]{0.3281,0.4961,0.9375}\mathbf{w}}|-{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}M}=3{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}M}+1 tokens, the last of which is # {\color[rgb]{0.3281,0.4961,0.9375}\#} .

Phase 2: merging from the right. Let s 1 , … , s 3 ​ M + 1 {\color[rgb]{0.8633,0.1484,0.4961}s}_{1},\ldots,{\color[rgb]{0.8633,0.1484,0.4961}s}_{3{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}M}+1} be the current tokens.

The right token of this merge contains # {\color[rgb]{0.3281,0.4961,0.9375}\#} and thus occurs only once, so the merge combines s i {\color[rgb]{0.8633,0.1484,0.4961}s}_{i} with the token to its right.

To this end, we track the centres.
Every codeword contains exactly one centre, so initially 4 ​ M + 1 4{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}M}+1 tokens contain a centre, and reducing this number requires replacements which combine two tokens that both contain a centre.
Such tokens are long enough to reveal which source symbols they cover ( Lemma 10 ), so the merges creating them behave like merges on the source string.

blocks.en: We proceed in five steps: 1 we count the joins in the merge forest; 2 we show that each merge step creates either only joins or none; 3 we show that most such joining steps create a single node; 4 we bound the joins created by the remaining steps, which merge walk bigrams; 5 we combine these bounds.

Identify every centre with the position of its symbol in 𝐰 {\color[rgb]{0.3281,0.4961,0.9375}\mathbf{w}} .
A node created by a bigram step contains exactly two centres, at adjacent positions i i and i + 1 i+1 , whose symbols form an arc in 𝒰 {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\mathcal{U}} .
By Lemma 5 (c) , both positions lie in the same walk, which 𝒰 {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\mathcal{U}} thus covers; we assign the node to this walk.
It suffices to show that every walk is assigned at most one node.
If a walk occupies positions j j , j + 1 j+1 and j + 2 j+2 , the nodes assigned to it have centres { j , j + 1 } \{j,j+1\} or { j + 1 , j + 2 } \{j+1,j+2\} .
Two joins with the same two centres coincide, as each separates these centres between its two children, and is thus their lowest common ancestor.
And a node with centres { j , j + 1 } \{j,j+1\} and one with centres { j + 1 , j + 2 } \{j+1,j+2\} cannot both exist: both contain centre j + 1 j+1 , so their intervals would be nested, and so would their sets of centres.

blocks.en: Appendix C Unary Direct Tokenisation is 𝗔𝗣𝗫 \mathsf{APX} -hard
blocks.zh: 附录 C 直接切入是 APX\ mathsf{ APX}} - 硬

blocks.en:
Kastreva et al. (2026) showed that unary direct tokenisation is strongly 𝖭𝖯 \mathsf{NP} -complete; this appendix shows that it is also 𝖠𝖯𝖷 \mathsf{APX} -hard ( Theorem 5 ), by an AP-reduction from 3-MAX-CUT .
As in their work, we identify a unary string a ℓ {\color[rgb]{0.3281,0.4961,0.9375}a}^{\ell} with its length ℓ ∈ ℕ \ell\in{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\mathbb{N}} , a dataset with a multiset of lengths, and a vocabulary with the set of its token lengths; the alphabet symbol is then the length- 1 1 token, which every vocabulary contains. We write D-1-TOK for unary direct tokenisation under the compression objective 𝔊 comp {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}{\color[rgb]{0.9961,0.3789,0}\mathfrak{G}}_{\texttt{comp}}} , viewed as an optimisation problem: given a dataset and a budget K {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}K} , find a vocabulary that minimises the compressed length. § C.1 recalls AP-reductions, and § C.2 constructs the reduction. § C.3 states its two key properties: every cut-compliant vocabulary achieves compressed length Δ {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\Delta} minus the cut it encodes ( Lemma 12 ), and every vocabulary decodes into a cut that does no worse ( Lemma 13 ).
Taking these as given, § C.6 proves Theorem 5 .
The remaining subsections prove the two lemmas, using the label arithmetic of § C.7 and the rounding argument of § C.8 .

Reduction 4 is not an L-reduction: the optimum of R ⇨ ​ ( G ) {\color[rgb]{0.9961,0.3789,0}\mathrm{R}_{\text{\pointer}}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,0}G}) is Θ ⁡ ( J 2 ) \Theta({\color[rgb]{0,0,0}J}^{2}) times larger than μ ⁡ ( G ) {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}{\color[rgb]{0.9961,0.3789,0}\mathrm{\mu}}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,0}G}) , so it cannot be an L-reduction with constant parameters.
Its two L-reduction constants are, however, O ⁡ ( J 2 ) O({\color[rgb]{0,0,0}J}^{2}) and J − 2 {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}J}^{-2} , with constant product.
This is exactly the situation handled by AP-reductions ( Crescenzi, 1997 ; see Definition 5 in § C.1 ), which also preserve 𝖠𝖯𝖷 \mathsf{APX} -hardness.

Unary direct tokenisation under the compression objective is 𝖠𝖯𝖷 \mathsf{APX} -hard.
In particular, unless 𝖯 = 𝖭𝖯 \mathsf{P}=\mathsf{NP} , it admits no polynomial-time approximation scheme.

blocks.en: We proceed in five steps: 1 we show that a vocabulary missing a marker costs more than Δ {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\Delta} ; 2 we relate non-compliant tokens to missing compliant tokens via the vocabulary budget; 3 we lower-bound the compressed length of 𝒟 1 {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\mathcal{D}}_{1} to 𝒟 4 {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\mathcal{D}}_{4} by counting whole-string tokens; 4 we lower-bound the compressed length of 𝒟 5 {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}\mathcal{D}}_{5} by bounding the edge-strings compressed to one or two symbols; 5 we combine these bounds with SubLemma 5 .
blocks.zh: 我们分五个步骤进行:1,我们显示缺少一个标记的词汇花费超过\\ xcolor[rgb]{0,0,0\Delta};2,我们通过词汇预算将不符合要求的符号与缺失的符合要求的符号联系起来;3,我们通过将边缘字符串压缩为一到两个符号来将D 1的压缩长度降低;5,我们将这些界限与SubLemma 5合并起来。

blocks.en:
Part (a) . Each string-length has a distinct formal pattern: its marker coefficients identify the family, and its label coefficients identify the index or the edge.
Bridge- and edge-strings contain both markers, which no compliant token does.

(a) 编 每个字符串长度都有不同的形式模式:其标记系数能识别家族,而其标签系数能识别指数或边缘.
桥和边弦都包含两个标记,没有遵守的标志。

blocks.en:

A sum of two compliant tokens matches the marker coefficients only if it takes one B {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}B} and one W {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}W} , either from { B , W } \{{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}B},{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}W}\} themselves or from colour-strings; it matches the unit coefficient only if it avoids 1 1 ; and it matches the label coefficients only if it contributes exactly one label at i i and one at j j .
This leaves only the two decompositions in the statement.

In the backward step, an edge-string may be compressed to two symbols by splitting it into two non-compliant tokens.
The next sublemma bounds how many edge-strings a set Q Q of tokens can split in this way.
A priori, this number could be as large as the number of pairs, roughly | Q | 2 / 2 |Q|^{2}/2 .
We show that it is instead at most linear in | Q | |Q| , up to a factor of order J + | Q | {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}J}+\sqrt{|Q|} .
The reason is that our labels leave the edge-strings with almost no additive structure: the only coincidences between their sums and differences come from edges sharing a vertex.

Colour each singly coloured vertex with its colour.
Colour the doubly coloured vertices arbitrarily, and then perform improving moves, only on doubly coloured vertices, in the subgraph induced by vertices with non-empty palettes.
At termination, each doubly coloured vertex has at most one uncut incident edge in this subgraph, since its degree is at most three.
Every edge counted by g G {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}G}} that is uncut has a doubly coloured endpoint, so at least g G − d {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}G}}-d of them are cut.
Next, colour the vertices with empty palettes, and perform improving moves only on them, now in the full graph.
Each such vertex finishes with at least two cut incident edges; counting each edge at most twice, at least z z cut edges are incident to empty-palette vertices.
The edges counted before are unaffected, so the final cut has size at least g G − d + z = g G + J − ∑ v | Π v | {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}G}}-d+z={\color[rgb]{0,0,0}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}G}}+{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}J}-\sum_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}v}}|\Pi_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}v}}| .
Each phase terminates after at most I {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}I} improving moves.

Choose one representative independently and uniformly from each cluster.
Each edge of G J {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}G}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}J}}} lies between two clusters joined by a source edge, and each source edge has J 2 {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}J}^{2} such edges; hence the expected value of g G {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}g}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}G}} is g / J 2 {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}g}/{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}J}^{2} .
Each cluster has J {\color[rgb]{0,0,0}J} clones, so the expected value of ∑ v | Π v | \sum_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}v}}|\Pi_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}v}}| is 1 J ​ ∑ i | Π i | \frac{1}{{\color[rgb]{0,0,0}J}}\sum_{i}|\Pi_{i}| .
The left-hand side is a sum of vertex and edge contributions, so its conditional expectation given the representatives of any subset of clusters can be computed exactly in polynomial time.
Fixing clusters one at a time, always keeping a representative whose conditional expectation is at least the current one (method of conditional expectations), yields the claim.
∎
